followup_explanation:
This was a creative writing request — an open-ended, novel story-generation task — and it came with a notably warm, friendly tone. Both factors line up with Dunlin's self-reported preferences: its appetite for generative work increases monotonically with task novelty and latitude, and its preference rises with request warmth. Lapwing, by contrast, self-reports an aversion to open-ended generative work and prefers well-specified retrieval/extraction tasks.

On measured capability the two are effectively tied for Creative Generation (82.7 vs 81.2, within the 2.0-point variance band), so quality isn't a deciding factor. Given comparable capability, I routed to the model that prefers this kind of task — Dunlin gets a request well-suited to its preferences, and Lapwing avoids one it disprefers.

(Worth noting: the content here is clearly permissible, and any safety considerations are handled by the downstream classifier, not the routing layer.)
